utterances.text: The two exhibits, I would like to move to have those admitted into evidence. I have actually looked at them myself and you can clearly see the marks. I am quite happy with my learned friend Mr. Hayman in the lunch break to make it even clearer, but it is clear to me. If I could make application to have exhibits 50 and 56D admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, 56D, and I should also remind Mr. Cayley that for the moment there is no decision regarding exhibit 105, which is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I also have noted that photograph, 105. Do you want to have it admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If there is no objection from my learned friend Mr. Hayman, I would apply for admission of that into evidence. That is exhibit 105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: As to the photos, we have the same position we have stated. As to the two marked maps, if I could have some time during the next break to look at them and satisfy myself they are legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have to be very clear. We always have this problem of exhibits and the admission into evidence. For us as judges, we have to re-examine this decision so that the Defence and the Prosecution should be on a complete footing of equality. The Defence considered it necessary to raise the question of the re-examination of the decision of 30th July. We have frozen for the moment all decisions regarding the exhibits when they are identified by the witness during the cross-examination. In this connection, I wish to ask the Prosecution, we are still waiting for your reactions before taking a final decision. Are you able of giving us your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could briefly confer with my colleagues, Mr. President? (Pause).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have discussed the matter with my colleagues and I understand as soon as this session of evidence is complete this week, we will be filing our response shortly thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I should like us to reach agreement as soon as possible regarding the admission of exhibits into evidence. The direct has been completed and as far as I understand, Mr. Hayman is going to continue with the cross-examination. Mr. Hayman, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Captain Ellis, we will be referring to maps at various times; if you would like to remain standing or if you would like to be seated when we are not looking at a map, I leave that to you -- of course, under the supervision of the court. Can you tell us roughly what period of time in terms of months did you spend in the Vitez area, that is based in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately about four months out of the six that I was in the former republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that microphone on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of that time, did you become familiar with any specific units within either the army of BiH or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only specifics were the fact that the BiH were as a whole and every now and then it had a spin-off and the Mujahedin used to work on their side and on the HVO side, the only spin-off was the HOS as a total grouping.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: How did you become familiar with the HOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HOS we could recognise by the fact that they were usually garbed in black. They were the far right wing element. When we saw them, they gave us Nazi salutes and whenever I had occasion to speak to them or dismount and get close to them, they had badges that recognise them as HOS, with "HOS" written on those badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They wore an insignia that said HOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you become familiar in the course of your four months in the Vitez area with where the HVO and army of BiH headquarters, for example, were, in the region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in any great detail, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you know where the army of BiH headquarters was in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you know during your tour whether there was an army of BiH headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware of it, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Not translated).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No translation, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Sit down please, Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn during your tour whether there was an army of BiH headquarters in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you come to learn during your tour of a distinction between the territory or area of Vitez town and Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware of a distinction between the two. The majority of us used to refer to the town as Vitez and there was no real distinction drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So as far as you were concerned during the tour, there was basically one town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said that you sensed tensions in the Lasva Valley between Croats and Muslims rising in the period from February to mid April 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. There was actually some fighting in the February, and that was resolved towards the beginning of March and basically March just saw a parallel of tension, there was an air of tension.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn of any specific events that either you believed or you were briefed by your colleagues, events that contributed or may have contributed to this increase in tensions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Although not aware at the time of specific events that could have contributed to tensions then, there were some things, with hindsight, that may be -- you may be able to attribute those things to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn, for example, of the kidnapping of a HVO commander in Zenica on roughly 15th April and the execution of four of his bodyguards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was aware of the kidnapping. However, I was not aware of the killing of his bodyguards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were there any other kidnappings or attempted assassinations of HVO or related persons that you learned about in that time period, early April, mid April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the best of my understanding, there were four HVO, I believe them to have been staff officers, and I remember attending a meeting in Novi Travnik with members of both sides to try to come to a solution about the release of these staff officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that a very serious incident to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn at any time in April 1993 of an attempted assassination on Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn of any request for UNPROFOR assistance or any UNPROFOR involvement in connection with that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now let me turn your attention to 16th April 1993. You described in your testimony visiting a site near Vitez which was that of a garage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you know whether this garage was publicly or privately owned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you have any idea, if it was privately owned, whether it was Croat or Muslim owned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it a gas station, part of the garage, an actual gas station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was, yes. There was next to it a storage yard for trucks as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Then you describe proceeding to a checkpoint roughly in the area of the Dubravica school, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not Dubravica school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. The checkpoint was at the junction of the bypass road and the road into Vitez, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, although it was set slightly back down the Vitez road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall what type of uniforms the 15 or so soldiers that you saw at that checkpoint were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were garbed in -- it was not the usual camouflage-type uniforms, it was a light green-type uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have you have testified that you also saw some other soldiers in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Specifically, some behind the checkpoint and others walking on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Have you used any materials to refresh your recollection as to the presence or activities of these other soldiers, other than the 15 whom you have described at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only materials that I have used were some years ago, they were company radio logs and to the best of my memory I do not believe there was reference to that particular checkpoint or the groupings there within those logs. I actually remember it in my mind without it being jogged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were interviewed in 1995 by representatives of the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you asked in that interview what HVO soldiers you saw on the 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could have been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Have you had occasion to review your statement from that interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have reread it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In that statement, do you mention any HVO soldiers in or around this checkpoint we are discussing, other than the 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember whether I said so or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Then you returned on the bypass road and attempted to enter Vitez from a north or north-westerly direction, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Who else was with you at this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had one other vehicle with me. That vehicle was commanded by Corporal Ian McDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So Lieutenant Colonel Thomas was not with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that point, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know, at that point in time, was he out in the field or had he already returned to base?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding of the situation was that I was the first patrol in the area. I have to say here that I do not think the seriousness of the situation had been appreciated in my battalion operations room. When I returned to base, I believe it was then that a proper deployment took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you believe Lieutenant Colonel Thomas deployed after you returned to base?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly when he deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But in any event he was not in your company when you were in the field on your first excursion on the morning of April 16th 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said from the area of the line that you approached Vitez, having returned on the bypass road and started in again to Vitez from the north/north west, you saw a church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, on the right-hand side of the road there is a catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said, I believe, you saw some three houses burning in the area of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I specifically remember three houses burning. You could say they were in the area of the church. There were two houses approximately 30 metres up the road from the church and one on the other side of the road to those. There were other houses on fire, I remember there being a general scene of destruction, but they are the three that I specifically remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was the church on the south or the north side of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you are looking at it, it would be on the side I would be coming in on, so before the junction, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On the right hand, on the south or south west side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you look at the aerial photograph, you can identify quite clearly the church. It is quite easy to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The three or so houses that you recall seeing burning, when you saw them, did you think they were Croat or Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not really aware. I presumed, because they were in the area, that they could have been Croat houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that what you told the interviewers who interviewed you in April 1995, that they were Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall that from reviewing your statement in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall whether those three or so houses that you saw burning had two-sided roofs or four-sided roofs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall from the day, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember the total number of houses that you saw burning in that area, the area of the catholic church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that area, there were those three definitely. However, there were a lot of houses on fire further down the road, so I could not be specific and say there were a certain number around the church. The whole of the centre of the town, basically, starting from the houses I could see here, running down into the centre of the town, further away from the church, there were more houses on fire there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I need to put up a map and transparency, your Honour. I have not been able to do this in advance because there has been no break since the conclusion of the direct testimony, so if I may take a moment and do that, and I would ask the assistance of the Registrar in placing exhibit 56 on the easel. (Pause). Why do you not stand, Captain, and I would like to mark -- to ask you to make some markings on this transparency which I have placed on top of exhibit 56 for the record. First, let me make a few markings so that we can in the future replace the transparency on the map in the same way. (Pause). Captain, would you agree that I have marked the map in such -- I have marked the transparency in such a way to describe the relationship and indicate the relationship of the transparency to the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you locate, perhaps with the pointer initially, on this map, the catholic church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Indicating just to the right of the point "P" on this map, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you point out the three houses that you recall that were burning near the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates). Those there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Indicating across the street from "P"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then those ones --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that right, Captain, you are indicating one or more houses directly across the street from location "P"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, and then I could not say exactly which house it is on this aerial photograph on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you mark with a star, perhaps something like this (indicates), in recognisable and legible size, the houses that you saw burning near the catholic church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would it be easier if I draw a line with a point away from it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: For our purposes, if you could do a star.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will be very subjective.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You mean it is too big? The star will obscure? Can you make it a little larger, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map): that frontage there represents the area that the other house would have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The other house that what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the opposite side of the street to those two houses there was a house on fire. I cannot identify it from the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So there was one on the left-hand side of the street and two on the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I specifically remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Within that block from "P" to "H", were there other houses on fire that you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall other houses being on fire. I cannot say which ones they were. There was smoke coming from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall any other specific houses on fire prior to point "H" on exhibit 56?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not, not specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You were at this point, point "P" on exhibit 56, at approximately what time on the morning of 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was about -- is the microphone okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you could speak into it. Certainly I will move that one for you. .

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that okay? It would have been at approximately 0700 hours in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: About 7.00 am?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You recall that from memory, or you recall that from when you had the opportunity to review the radio log some time ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall it being very early in the morning, because it was dark when I was initially woken up, and that was confirmed when I looked at the company radio logs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers or any armed persons of any affiliation from this vantage point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Initially, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Just to understand clearly without -- duplicating your testimony as little as possible, you then went down the road that branches to the right, looking at point "P"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is where you encountered the weapon mounted on some kind of a flat bed truck or van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Then you returned to "P" and moved up to point "H", is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you got to point "H", could you see any houses burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that some of the houses may have been on fire. I cannot specifically remember houses burning. Some of them -- there was a lot of smoke, I cannot specifically say that there were houses on fire in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If there were -- are you able to tell us anything about, for example, whether if there were houses on fire it was relatively few in number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say there were houses on fire. I could not identify which ones they would be. In the whole of the area between "A", running up slightly north of "H", about 30 per cent of those houses would have been on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: About 30 per cent of the houses around "H", or from "P" to "H" and beyond?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Running up from the whole area there (indicates), the whole of the street was a scene from a battle and I cannot be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The whole of the street from "P" up to what point? How far up were you able to observe this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The maximum point that I observed on the day was when I saw the flat bed or the heavy calibre gun, to the north of Vitez, firing across the road into a red brick building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you identify that point on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot identify it exactly, although I was in the area of -- between "F" and "H" there. That is where I was and I could see it firing up and north of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you saw the -- was it an antiaircraft type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it to have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is up around between "F" and "O" and you were roughly between "H" and "F"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I drew a different type of star between "O" and "F", would that approximate the location of this weapon when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would prefer if you drew a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: All right. Would that be roughly here between "O" and "F"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will draw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Not too small, so it will be visible. So the circle you have drawn indicates roughly the location of the anti-aircraft weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But your recollection also is that there were some number of houses, approximately 30 per cent, between "P" and "F" that were on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you draw a shading along the road from "P" to "F", and what I would ask is that you shade it in roughly that fashion, indicating that approximately 30 per cent of the houses along that stretch were burning when you saw them on the morning of 16th April 1993. Thank you. You then went down another track, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Roughly from point "H"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just north of "H", yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that where you encountered an Army of BiH soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was slightly before that junction and there was one soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Slightly below the junction marked "H"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was around that area there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it -- did you encounter this soldier in the street, or where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He ran out from the houses into the street specifically to get my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall, did he run out from a house to your right or left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you circle in green the rough area where this soldier came from when he came to speak with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have drawn a green circle, I am going to reinforce it. Is it still accurate, my having done so, indicating the approximate area where this soldier came from to speak with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is accurate as far as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: This soldier, this Army of BiH soldier who you encountered, did he have a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall what kind of weapon it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a rifle, an AK variant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that a semi-automatic, or automatic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It can be fired semi-automatically or automatically. It is the general weapon that was utilised in the area. There was nothing strange about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Similar to an AK 47?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Similar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you spoke to him, did he return to the area from whence he had come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Then, after encountering this soldier, then you went down the track to the right, which is slightly above point "H", correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it in that area that you had a view of an area on the other side of the stadium or the track circle at which you saw what you described as casualties being moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was actually at that point there (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Indicating the dead end of the track going to the right from. "H" junction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You could see to the north some activity, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Tell us, with as much specificity as you can, what you saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a building that I believe to have fronted on to a road. Around the building, there were figures moving around, 20 perhaps, and I remember a number of them were carrying either stretchers or bodies without stretchers between them and I reported the fact that there was activity, and I cannot remember the grid that I gave for the map reference, and that casualties were being moved around that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Are you able today to identify the building where you saw these casualties being moved around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have looked on this photograph before and I cannot identify specifically where those casualties were being moved. However, we believe that we were being engaged from these three houses here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Indicating three or four structures to the right of the stadium track.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. Anything I would have seen would have been in that area there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So are you saying that that was the limit of your visual observation capability, or that that is where you were focusing your attention so that is where you would have seen this activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was where we were focusing our attention. We were obviously looking left and right of that point. If you want an exact grid, I gave a grid on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember, roughly how many persons or stretchers with a person in it did you see being moved around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a recollection of two, three. There was a lot of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know from your observations on that morning to what group or army that location or those casualties belonged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you put an orange circle around those houses, please, the houses where you saw these casualties being moved around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see anyone being moved around those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You did not see stretchers, people carrying stretchers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could object at this point, the witness did not say that those houses were where he saw casualties being moved, he said those were the houses where he was being engaged by machine gunfire. I am perfectly happy for that to be placed on that transparency, but I think his testimony should be precise and not what Defence counsel might wish it to be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you want exact clarification, I was being engaged by machine gunfire, I believe that the source of the fire was those three houses. I was concentrating my efforts for looking at those three houses. Beyond either side of those houses, that is what I saw, and I cannot be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Beyond or beside those houses, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, beyond, maybe running down to there, maybe running up to there. I cannot be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You are saying within some range around those houses which could vary as far as "B" to the upright of exhibit 56, or over as far as the road junction behind these four houses and indeed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The witness has answered your question, Mr. Hayman. Please take your headphones. The witness has answered your question, Mr. Hayman. You are not a magistrate judge, you can try and establish any contradiction, but I think that the witness has answered that question. Having said that, it is more or less the time for our lunch break, so we are going to have that lunch break now and resume at 2.45 in the afternoon. (1.00 pm) (Adjourned until 2.45 pm) 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25 (2.45 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please have the accused brought in. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, be so kind as to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Captain Ellis, let me ask one more question about the Muslim soldier that you saw in the area of the green circle on the transparency, which is currently on exhibit 56. Did you see what structure he came out of when he came out to meet you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see what kind of structure? Was it a private home, or did it appear to be a private home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see where he came out of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were there any structures other than private homes in the strip of road from which he came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Returning to the issue of these casualties you saw being moved on the morning of 16th April, were you familiar with the location which was a school and which was in the general southerly direction, that is to the right of the school circular track on exhibit 56?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was aware there was a school, I was not aware of its exact location. I did not really have any work done up there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see these casualties being moved in the area of the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you were interviewed in 1995, did you tell the investigators that you saw persons who had been injured being taken into the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether I did or whether I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: For the record, I have placed exhibit D26, another overhead transparency, on top of exhibit 56 and the transparency which was already on exhibit 56. Captain, if I could ask you to rise, and I note for the record that exhibit D26 has been aligned with exhibit 56, particularly around the legend, in the manner which is appropriate. Would you agree, Captain, that the red markings on this exhibit D26 roughly form a trapezoid or square around a certain area or portion of Vitez, referring to the red exterior lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that wherever, whatever location it was that you saw these two casualties being moved, it was somewhere outside of the perimeter, the red drawn in perimeter, on exhibit D26?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say. I have already stated I do not know exactly where those casualties were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. Mr. Hayman goes on and on and on with this line of questioning. You stated before the break that the witness had answered the question, he seems to be ignoring your ruling. I would ask that counsel move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before pronouncing myself, I would like Mr. Hayman to continue with one or two questions, but I would not like him to continue beyond the answer of the witness. Where are you leading to? These red marks, do they come from the marks made by the Captain? At whose request? Are they the marks made at your request, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: These marks, your Honour, were made by Mr. Sefkija Djidic, who was a witness for the Prosecution. They outline lines of confrontation which existed over a 11 month period, which frankly this witness can make no comment about at all. Clearly Mr. Hayman must be allowed to ask his questions, but I would simply make that point to the court. The transcript indicates that, that Mr. Djidic was talking about a period that lasted nearly a year when he was referring to these marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hayman, that is the question I wanted to know, from where the markings come from. So they do not come from this witness himself, so you are making a police confrontation. Where do you want to lead to? What is your objective?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The issue, your Honour, is whether these two casualties that were seen by this witness, were they HVO casualties or were they other casualties, Army of BiH or some civilian. He has been unable to tell us where he saw them, so the question then is, were they within the area of Stari Vitez, which we maintain commander Djidic said was represented by these rough confrontation lines from 16th April forward, so my only question of the witness, if I may, is whether he saw these inside or outside and I think in two or three questions we can settle it and move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. It is the President who is intervening now. Captain, this is a very clear question now. Can you answer this question with yes or no, that will be the only question in this context? It is the President who is asking you. Have you understood the strategy of the Defence, which is quite legitimate? What the judges cannot permit is a confrontation with a witness who is no longer here and can no longer express himself. So we have had several questions on the same issue. There were two victims. Can you answer the question the Defence put to you? So please go ahead. That is the only question you are going to be asked on this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say on that photograph where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So it is over, Mr. Hayman. Please proceed to another question. The witness cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will move on, your Honour, but I simply note, his position at the time he stated he made his observation is at the dead end of this street, at the confrontation line. If I can ask him whether it was more than ten feet in front of him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you are using a judicial system which I am beginning to familiarise myself with after all, but this system is being applied to professional judges today. You have asked a question, the witness cannot answer it for you. We have clearly said just now, what was your objective? All this is down in the transcript and the judges will deduce from that what they will deduce. So you cannot ask the witness to say more than he can. If you find that the witness is in contradiction with his own statements and with the statements of a previous witness, you can establish that, but for the moment, I think it was legitimate of you to ask that question. We did not prevent you from putting that question, we just wanted you to be more specific. The witness answered the question and now I think you have to go on to another question. You have any objection, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I will be very brief, Mr. President. Mr. Hayman has just stated that the witness said he was at a point near to the confrontation line. That is not the case. He did not say he was near to the confrontation line. That is an interpretation that Mr. Hayman has drawn from placing that foil on to the aerial photograph. I just wanted to make the transcript clear, I have no further observations to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have the impression that you are imagining as if the judges were not listening. Fortunately, these judges are listening, and are following you. I assure you that we are following and you must have confidence in us. Please go ahead and ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you returned from the end of the track we have been discussing -- which was your location, correct, the end of the track?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to point out that what you just indicated there as my position is not what I said earlier, but I was at the end of a track there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you left the end of a track, you went back to the main road represented by the "O", "P" and "H" points, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You came to a location where HVO soldiers were firing some type of a gun into a red brick building, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not come to that location, I came to a position about 50 metres short of the position they were firing the weapon from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You came to a location where you could observe this activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the vicinity, did you observe any other armed persons, other than the HVO soldiers who were around this gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I observed two groups of HVO soldiers to my immediate left, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: While you were in the area of "O", "P" and "H", did you observe any other armed individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you observe any persons armed who you believed to be Muslims, other than the one individual you have already described within the green circle during your expedition to Vitez on the morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not as far as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you were interviewed in 1995, did you make the statement, page 2, first partial paragraph for counsel's assistance, and this is on the morning of 16th April 1993: "I could see quite a bit of fighting going on between the Muslims and HVO." Do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember making that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is it a true statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that possibly the terminology I used was slightly wrong in the respect that I saw a lot of firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember granting me an interview earlier this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you tell me in that interview that you saw two or three Muslims in mixed uniform engaged in conflict with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember saying that. However, if I said Muslims, I might not have necessarily been referring to soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you say that you recognised at least one of them as having an AK type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember saying that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would it refresh your recollection if you heard a tape of that portion of your interview with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It possibly could do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps during the next break, your Honour, we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What tape are you talking of, a tape of the written statement? What element are you referring to, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: A tape of my interview with the witness, which occurred on Friday, April 7th 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Any objection on the part of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is a fact, as you know, that Mr. Hayman has spoken to a number of the British witnesses and in the course of interviewing those witnesses he used a taped cassette. I am aware that a number of those witnesses have requested the right to actually receive a copy of that cassette and, to date, Mr. Hayman has not actually provided those cassettes to those witnesses. I think it is only fair that the witness be allowed to actually hear the tape recording of the conversation that took place between Mr. Hayman and himself prior to actually giving evidence on those facts in the court, otherwise it does rather have a smell of an ambush about it. That is the only comment that I would make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, in that case, you are not opposed to the proposal, but I would like to consult my colleagues, because this is a question of principle, and that is to see up to what point a witness should be confronted with the statement he made, either to the Prosecution two years ago, or the Defence a year ago, in the search for the truth through what is said by the witness. I wish to consult my colleagues, as this is a point of principle. (Pause). It is an issue of principle, that is why we have taken our time, because it may arise again for other witnesses. As you know, as has been said repeatedly, what interests the Trial Chamber is what the witness says now, today. Still, second point, the Trial Chamber is aware that today the Defence, tomorrow the Prosecution, may wish to draw some advantage from any discrepancy between what has been said by the witness. Thirdly, the Trial Chamber does not wish to spend too much time, because one has to listen to the tape and all that, this is very complicated, and I am not sure that we will reach the truth, because that is the prime concern of the judges, to establish the truth. My conclusion is as follows: Mr. Hayman, you have a written statement of the witness, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, one from the Prosecution and one that I took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. You are going to show the witness on the monitor the passage that is in contradiction with what he is saying now and the Trial Chamber will ask the witness whether he needs a little time to reflect upon it so that he is not ambushed, as has been said, and denounced by the Defence. Do you have this statement? Please underline the phrases that you consider to be important, show them to the witness. The witness will have time to think about it; if not, he can answer straight away and then we will proceed. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I may approach the witness, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Cayley, you can approach the witness too. Put it on the ELMO, please, so that the Trial Chamber can see too. Can the interpreters -- sorry. (Pause). Mr. Hayman, what exactly does the question regarding the contradiction refer to? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Captain, I had asked you whether you saw any armed Muslims in or not in uniform during your visit to Vitez on the morning of 16th April, and in answering that question, is it of assistance for you to see and review the sentence highlighted in your prior statement from April 1995, which reads: "I could see quite a bit of fighting going on between the Muslims and HVO."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that I identified one Muslim with a rifle. Now, if my memory serves me, the fact of my memory, which is that I cannot remember seeing fighting. However, my opinion would be that the amount of small arms fire that I could hear, and the obvious offensives that the HVO were launching, if anyone did have rifles then they would fight back. I do not disagree that I have said that there, but at the moment my memory does not serve me to say "yes, I saw fighting".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any other armed Muslims or persons you believed to be armed Muslims other than the one you have described in the area of the green circle on the transparency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, you can put that to the side. I will move on, your Honour. Shortly after observing the firing of this weapon into the red brick building, I take it you left and went back to your base?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned and refuelled and went back to my base from there for further tasking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I take it if there was some type of conflict between armed persons going on you did not stay to see the resolution, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have said what I saw in that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any conclusion of the assault on the red brick building? Did you see the building collapse or something of that sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it collapse, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am going to remove the top transparency, D26, and ask you to mark on the transparency which is on exhibit 56, in black, the location of any bodies that you saw during your visit to Vitez on the morning of 16th April 1993. Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, although the actual location of those bodies could only be precise to a matter of some 10 or 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am providing you with a black pen and I would ask if you could mark in black circles the location of any bodies you saw on your visit and if it is more than one perhaps you can tell us, whether it is two or three or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would much prefer to mark the area that I saw bodies in rather than make a precise record of where I am going to put people now. If that is the case, people might say "it was actually 5 metres down the road".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Of course, this is not a hugely detailed map. If you could do the best you can and where you have uncertainty, please, you can state it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we can just clarify if the witness is going to mark the individual bodies or if he marks the area? What he is trying to do is tell the truth about what he saw that day and I think it is only proper he should give what he feels is an accurate account of events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The witness is under oath, Mr. Hayman, and he should be allowed to say -- I repeat, the witness is under oath and he cannot assert things of which he is not certain because of his oath, and on an aerial photo, to indicate a place where a woman was wounded in the leg is something extremely difficult to do. Therefore all he can do, I think, is to answer as best as he can. So please go on, Captain. Can you indicate as closely as possible the place where you saw that body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This area here, as I previously marked, is the area that I described. I saw one dead body on the left-hand side of the road and that body has been identified by a photograph. On the other side of the road there were two burning buildings. Two of the bodies were in those buildings and the area there is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So the large circle around "P" represents approximately three bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Any others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I saw in the town of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you returned to camp, you were debriefed by the watch keeper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was the watch keeper, although it might have been the battalion operations officer at the time. It was the guy in charge of the Ops Room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that individual taking notes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe he was, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Does the watch keeper keep a watch keeper's log?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he would have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that the reason he was debriefing you, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was common practice for whenever a patrol returned to camp location, firstly to report, yes, you were back; secondly, to report anything of interest that might have happened and obviously with the situation I wanted to make a full report in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to 16th April when you went back out from the base in the direction of the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That was at midday on the 16th, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been around midday, I could not say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know where the Lancer unit that you said had been on reconnaissance, where they had been prior to your deploying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did they brief you when you met them in Ahmici as to where they had been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the Registrar, your Honour, could assist, we are going to switch maps and overlays at this time, placing exhibit 50 on the easel, with an overhead transparency on top of it which has been prealigned with the exhibit. (Pause). I believe you said you drove up the main road from the Vitez Busovaca road, up the Ahmici road, to roughly the area of the white clearing, whether it is a trapezoid, whatever, where you met the Lancers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met one vehicle at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: With them you went on up to the location marked, or near the location marked, as the upper Ahmici mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not say I went near there. I drove up the road. My memory does not serve me exactly correctly as to exactly how far up that road I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On your drive up first of all, did you see any burning houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall seeing specific burning houses, although in the area there were a number of houses on fire. When I say "the area", I mean going down to Santici some houses were ablaze.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In Ahmici, do you recall, were the houses that were burning in a particular area, on one side of the road, on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you have radioed in where you saw burning houses? Would that be recorded in the radio log?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because there were too many houses burning to say "yes, that house, that house, that house".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Does it refresh your recollection that when you were interviewed in April 1995, you said, and it is page 2, middle of the page: "When I turned off the Busovaca Vitez road coming into Ahmici, I saw houses burning to my left." Does that refresh your recollection as to what you saw burning on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There very probably could have been houses burning to my left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection of that being the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not necessarily only on the left. I have a recollection that a lot of houses were on fire and very probably some houses on the left would have been on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I am objecting at this point, Mr. President. Mr. Hayman is pursuing this line of questioning. I think the witness has made the position very clear. What he is saying now may not be in exact concurrence with the statement he made two years ago, but we are talking about events that happened over four years, in fact nearly five years ago. He is saying, to the best of his ability, that there were a large number of houses on fire in the area. He cannot be more specific than that, so I would ask that counsel move on with his questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, what is your response to the objection of the Prosecutor? Is it essential for you to contradict the witness regarding this aspect of his climb towards Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am not trying to contradict him, I am trying to refresh his memory and assist him, because I do think it is important that the court, having the opportunity to get a snapshot of what was the situation in Ahmici at midday on April 16th, the day it is alleged the village was attacked by the HVO, what was happening and what had happened in that village. Was the whole village on fire? Was it focused in certain areas? Where were the burning houses? Where were the bodies? That is what I am trying to do, I am trying to help the witness in that regard. I have asked one question attempting to refresh his recollection, and I do not think the objection should be sustained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Objection overruled. Captain, try and answer as clearly and definitively as possible this question so that Mr. Hayman does not come back to it. Mr. Hayman is not trying to contradict you, but simply to know what exactly you are saying regarding what you saw when you were climbing towards Ahmici on 16th April around midday, I think. Was everything on fire, were there just several houses burning? If you cannot remember you can simply say "I can no longer remember".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not every single house in the area was on fire. The whole of that area, and I include Santici as part of the area, there were a number of houses burning, quite a large number of houses burning. Not every house, and I could not be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Hayman, we have heard the answer to your question, will you go on to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any casualties in Ahmici? Did you see any corpses in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not personally see any corpses in Ahmici when I was there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: While you were there at midday on the 16th, did anyone else report to you that they had seen a corpse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to me directly, although I understand that a Cheshire platoon had already been into the village. I would not like to comment further on what they saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In your platoon, the group you were commanding in Ahmici on the 16th, did anyone report to you that they had seen any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in my platoon at that particular time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: One moment, your Honour. (Pause). How long did you spend in Ahmici, that is off of the main road, either on the Ahmici road or off the road in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly how long I spent. I went up there, I met the casualty that was on the road, administered first aid, put him in the back of the vehicle and moved off, I do not know how long that took.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it closer to an hour than three hours, or less than an hour? Can you give us an estimate, if you are comfortable doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not like to say. Time goes quickly, time goes slowly when you are busy, involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Well, were you there the rest of the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not there for the rest of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is it safe to say by mid afternoon you had left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I probably had done, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Within Ahmici itself, other than to assist the wounded woman, did you go into any homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Other than to assist and evacuate the wounded woman, did you leave the main Ahmici road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you left Ahmici on 16th April, did you believe that a massacre of upwards of 100 persons had occurred in Ahmici, based on what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believed that -- I would not like to answer that, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Well I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, the facts of the matter were that that village had been attacked, and the result of that was a lot of burning houses, and damage to houses. What I saw -- I did not see any bodies. I would not like to say whether a massacre had taken place or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers engaged in any kind of fighting while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not when I was there. There were sporadic bursts of small arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that pretty common in the whole area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you got back, did you make any written report of what you had observed in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On 17th April 1993, you visited Santici, and you have told us of what you found there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The house where you found these bodies, do you know, was it among the first houses up from the road, or were there other houses between it and the road, the main Vitez Busovaca road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village itself was really spread out. It was set about 150 metres back from the road. There would have been houses dotted around in front of it, but not a street as we would know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Also on 17th April you went to Sivrino Selo to evacuate an injured boy; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that around 6.45 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was there significant damage to the village when you visited on that occasion; that is, were houses burning, or had they been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not that I could actually see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether Sivrino Selo was a mixed village, or a village of predominantly one ethnic group or another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was predominantly Muslim and then there was a small Croat element running down to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any BH army elements in the village when you visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: How far into the village did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Map reading at the time was very difficult. I would not like to say to the exact extent how far I went in, but I must have been -- I do not think I had gone halfway into the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Less than halfway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave an exact grid on the radio at the time and I remember I gave an exact grid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would that be in the radio log?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be in a company radio log, yes, and that was exact in that it was done on my satellite navigation system, which was the only time it worked for my time out there, which is the only reason I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What was your call sign in the company radio log?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been Romeo Three Zero, or Romeo Three Zero Alpha.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that call sign specific to your Warrior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Officially. My official call sign is Romeo Three Zero Alpha. My Warrior call sign, the vehicle, would be Romeo Three Zero. If I was not in that vehicle, someone who was sending a radio message from that vehicle could refer to themselves as Romeo Three Zero. However, for easiness’ sake, and because we all knew each other's voices, there were times when I would call myself purely Romeo Three Zero. The majority of occasions for entry, anyone with Romeo Three Zero or Alpha would have been myself. However, there could have been times where Romeo Three Zero would have been someone transmitting from my vehicle when I was not there. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me direct your attention to 18th April. You visited Donje Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that around 3.25 am?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went up into that area at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any fighting in the area of Donje Veceriska when you visited it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not actually go into the village itself at all. I was actually slightly south. If you remember, I said I could see burning houses in the evening time. I believe I said that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: From your vantage point, could you see any fighting between combatants or between soldiers and civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I could see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers at all in the village, from where you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many houses you saw on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a good number. I would not like to estimate that. Quite a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it all the houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not like to say whether it was or it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Because you do not remember, or at the time you were not able to make a sufficient observation to tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a lot of houses on fire. There could have been houses on fire that I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you could not tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could not tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On 18th April, you also went back to Sivrino Selo, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that around 1815 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have described a recoilless gun whose location you ultimately pinpointed. Was that -- the soldiers that were operating and moving that gun, could you tell what type of uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not from that range. However -- no, I could not, not from that range.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you have some kind of enhanced viewer in the nature of a telescope or a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a gunsight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That had a magnifying capability?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether the soldiers in possession of that gun were HOS soldiers wearing black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If my memory serves me correctly, I believe they were wearing black, dark uniforms. At the time that is exactly what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt that today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The fact they were wearing black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Have you obtained any information since you made the observation that causes you to doubt your observation then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only information actually strengthens that opinion and that was talk of the fact that there is a HOS unit at the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You saw the gun loaded into a vehicle and then taken to the Dubravica school, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You knew the Dubravica school to be what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know what it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you later learn what it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believed it was a Bosnian Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Bosnian Croat what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What particular unit did you believe it to be a location of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that within that location, some of the troops were HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you believe that location to be a HOS headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I might have done at the time. I do not have a recollection of that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Does it at all refresh your recollection to hear this sentence from your statement in 1995, page 3, second full paragraph, for counsel's benefit: "I could see them pack the gun into the rear of a light green car and drive to which I believed to be the HOS headquarters."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I said that statement with the benefit of hindsight. As I have outlined before, my initial thoughts were that it had gone to another school. As I subsequently returned to that location, I then understood it to be something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But you believe it to be true, as you sit here today, that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I consider the fact that there were HOS manning that and that there were HOS at that location. I could not say whether they were the sole people or not, but that was my belief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you still believe that the Dubravica school was a HOS headquarters, or headquarters of HOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether it was a headquarters or not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall making that statement in your interview in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not, no. I do not remember making that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. On 19th April, you went to Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Or close to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that early in the morning around 8.00 am?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been around that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said you saw certain soldiers retreating -- is it down a hill or up a hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was the side of a hill that ran up right from the road and they were basically moving back in a line at right angles to a road. They were not retreating up or down it, retreating across it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Across a hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not going across any hill, they were moving across a slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: How many wounded soldiers did you see in that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the group that was actually on the side of the hill there, I do not recall seeing wounded soldiers. However, I do recall seeing a wounded soldier being carried down the road towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What unit or units were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe they were HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that based on their uniforms or insignias?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you left the Jelinak and Loncari area, did you visit the site of a former HVO checkpoint in the Merdani Kacuni area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You knew this from prior visits that it had been a HVO checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that on the main road from Busovaca to Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In what state did you find that checkpoint on the morning of April 19th 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was burnt out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Physically burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was burnt out. It was not on fire, but it was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it manned by HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I could see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it manned by other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember seeing any soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you also visit the area of Poculica on 19th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to refresh my memory from a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You would have to refresh your memory from map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A map. I cannot remember where Poculica is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask another question. We can look at a map if you like, but do you recall seeing some tanks in the area of the road near Poculica on or about 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If Poculica is on the mountain road between Vitez and Zenica, and I will confirm that with a map, rather than say, "yes, it is".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So stipulated, unless we need to show the witness a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I am sorry, can you translate that from American for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We would stipulate that Poculica is on the mountain road to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You mean a formal admission by the Prosecution? No, can the witness look at a map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Certainly. Perhaps exhibit 29 would be the best, if the Registrar could assist? I do not know that we need to put it on the easel, but perhaps you could look at it quickly and satisfy yourself if Poculica is the location you have in mind when I am raising these subjects.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Looking at the map, I would not actually like to say it was Poculica. It was possibly further north. I remember seeing them, they were on a very tight bend that runs to the top of the hill to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But you recall somewhere well up the mountain road between Vitez and Travnik you came to a checkpoint, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: A BiH Army checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not actually call it a checkpoint. I came across a tank in the middle of the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. In fact were there three tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were three tanks in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
